issue_context.title: StreamContent.ReadOnlyStream fails Stream conformance tests
issue_context.body:
[`StreamContent`'s stream implementation](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a361f7f84ac627b34a611be89b52d9dc75293bbf/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/StreamContent.cs#L139) does not pass [`StreamConformanceTests`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a361f7f84ac627b34a611be89b52d9dc75293bbf/src/libraries/Common/tests/StreamConformanceTests/System/IO/StreamConformanceTests.cs#L22).

Some issues:
- [`WriteTimeout`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a361f7f84ac627b34a611be89b52d9dc75293bbf/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/StreamContent.cs#L148) should throw an `InvalidOperationException` instead of `NotSupportedException`
- [`Flush(Async)`](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a361f7f84ac627b34a611be89b52d9dc75293bbf/src/libraries/System.Net.Http/src/System/Net/Http/StreamContent.cs#L157-L165) should no-op instead of throwing

We should fix the above two issues and consider writing a stream conformance test for this stream.

review_comments:
Shouldn't we implement `WriteTimeout` explicitly as well?
As far as I can tell the test is currently using `MemoryStream` as the inner stream, so this ends up in the base `Stream`'s impl which throws the expected `InvalidOperationException`. With an arbitrary `Stream` I assume we want to guard against this being set?

> With an arbitrary Stream I assume we want to guard against this being set?

I don't think we need to.  There's no harm in setting a write timeout if you can't write.

If you get the stream from `StreamContent`, you can't write to it. But something else in the process could be if they have access to the stream used to create the content, and seeing the `WriteTimeout` change may be unexpected.

That said, I don't think this matters realistically for this stream since there's no reason to set the timeout if all the writes will throw anyway.
I don't think it's necessary, but I also don't think it matters either way.  I put it back.
